name: Auralis Core
known_drawback: Very low price comes with a basic plastic build; some owners report hinge looseness and noticeable battery aging after heavy use. The microphone is also weak in noisy places.
review_pattern: Reviews often praise the price and light weight, but long-term owners are less positive about durability and battery consistency.
plain_language_notes: A very cheap, lightweight option. It works well enough for casual use, but the low price shows up in build quality, calls, and long-term durability.

name: Velora One
known_drawback: Excellent battery life, but noise cancellation is modest and the earcups do not block much sound passively.
review_pattern: Owners consistently like the runtime; commuters are more divided because outside noise remains noticeable.
plain_language_notes: A strong battery-focused choice. It is practical for long days, but it is not designed to be the quietest option on a bus or flight.

name: Sonex Lite
known_drawback: Very comfortable for long sessions, but the microphone struggles in busy environments and the sound is tuned more for general listening than detail.
review_pattern: Study and music users rate the comfort highly; work-call users are more mixed.
plain_language_notes: Comfort is the main reason to buy it. It is easy to wear for hours, but it is not the strongest choice if calls or highly detailed music matter.

name: Novara Pro
known_drawback: Near-top performance across most categories, but it is expensive and noticeably heavier than the lighter travel-focused models.
review_pattern: Reviewers praise its noise cancellation and sound; the main complaints are price and weight during very long travel days.
plain_language_notes: A premium all-rounder: excellent isolation and sound, good comfort, but you pay substantially more and carry a heavier headset.

name: EchoSphere S
known_drawback: Strong overall package, although its touch controls can register accidental taps when adjusting the headphones and the design is fairly plain.
review_pattern: Most owners see it as dependable everyday equipment; accidental touch inputs are the recurring annoyance.
plain_language_notes: A balanced middle-ground choice with few major weaknesses. The main practical annoyance is accidental touch input while adjusting the earcups.

name: ZenTone Air
known_drawback: Extremely light and comfortable, but the short battery means frequent charging and the lightweight construction feels less substantial than the price suggests.
review_pattern: Long-session users love the fit; frequent travellers are much less enthusiastic about the battery.
best_for: people who prioritise comfort and lightness
plain_language_notes: The comfort champion. It almost disappears on your head, but that advantage comes with short battery life and a premium price.

name: PulseArc
known_drawback: Strong bass and eye-catching design, but voices and acoustic instruments can sound less natural; the fit is also less comfortable for some users after several hours.
review_pattern: Bass-heavy music fans tend to like it, while people who prefer balanced sound and long sessions are more divided.
plain_language_notes: Fun, energetic and stylish. It is a deliberate sound choice rather than a neutral all-rounder, and long-session comfort is only average.

name: Quieta Max
known_drawback: Excellent noise cancellation, but heavy ANC use reduces practical battery runtime and the bulkier earcups are less convenient to carry around.
review_pattern: Commuters praise the isolation; frequent travellers note that the case and larger earcups take up more space.
plain_language_notes: Built around strong noise reduction. It is excellent on noisy transport, but less attractive if compactness and maximum battery efficiency matter.

name: Travelleaf
known_drawback: Exceptional battery and low weight, but call quality is average and the sound is less detailed than the more expensive models.
review_pattern: Commuters like how easy it is to carry and how rarely it needs charging; music-focused reviewers are less impressed.
plain_language_notes: A practical travel companion. Its strengths are battery and portability, while sound detail and calls are the compromises.

name: StudioNest
known_drawback: Excellent sound quality, but the heavy build is awkward for travel and the high price only makes sense if audio quality is a major priority.
review_pattern: Audio-focused users praise the sound; casual listeners often question the price and weight.
plain_language_notes: The specialist choice for sound quality. It is expensive and heavy, so its strengths make the most sense for people who will actually use them.
